tasks.short: Observe and caution children around animals

steps.what: Observe children and animals and caution unsafe petting or feeding

tasks.design: Keep live observation and intervention with the caretaker. Existing instructions in {DOCS} can support training but do not replace attention to children or animals.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work requires immediate physical presence and situational judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated change to this task is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Behaviour changes quickly and a child may not understand a warning.
tasks.human_edge: Notice distress and intervene calmly before contact becomes unsafe.
tasks.altitude: The caretaker retains the same duty and decision rights.

evidence.claim: Retaining live supervision and assigning no time saving is a task design judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is supervision during visitor contact; training and visitor admission are outside it.
No structured input or automated decision is introduced.
No system change is proposed; native configuration is unnecessary and incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Animal species and visitor contact policy
research_questions: Which situations require a second caretaker to intervene?

already_counted.description: All observation and cautioning remains in s1

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net=0. Live visitor contact remains fully staffed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Discuss grooming needs, inspect coat condition and agree suitable care with clients

tasks.design: Keep the discussion and assessment with the caretaker. Species care sheets in {DOCS} may inform it, without replacing inspection or client agreement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preferences, coat condition and animal tolerance must be reconciled in conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted care information is available, but no reduction in this conversation is established.
tasks.still_hard: A requested style may conflict with comfort or safe handling.
tasks.human_edge: Explain limits kindly and agree a realistic grooming plan.
tasks.altitude: Client discussion remains part of the caretaker's week.

evidence.claim: LICG provides species-specific information on animal care, health and welfare; this does not establish grooming consultation savings.

assumptions: Boundary is the live grooming-needs discussion, excluding grooming delivery and appointment administration.
No structured input or automation is introduced.
No implementation is proposed; native configuration and incremental upkeep are unnecessary.
research_questions: Which preferences most often require an explanation of welfare limits?

already_counted.description: Client discussion and assessment retained in full

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and zero upkeep give net=0; no paperwork baseline is inferred from a conversation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order, unload and store feed and supplies

steps.what: Count usable stock and capture required feed and supplies
Enter order and confirm exact items, quantities, supplier and delivery
Unload delivery and verify feed condition and quantities
Store supplies under suitable conditions and rotate feed stock

tasks.design: Configure reusable approved catalogue lines in {PROCUREMENT} to reduce repeated order entry. The caretaker still counts stock, captures the request, approves the final order and physically receives and stores supplies.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated catalogue entry can coexist with stock checks that cannot be skipped.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved order lists can reuse item and supplier references.
tasks.still_hard: Diet changes, expiry, damaged bags and storage capacity require direct checks.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsuitable feed and preserve safe storage conditions.
tasks.altitude: A small amount of entry falls away; stock and animal-care responsibility stays the same.

evidence.claim: Native saved catalogue lines and the six-point gross saving are a conditional design scenario, not a measured animal-care case.

assumptions: Boundary includes caretaker counting, ordering, unloading and storage; supplier transport is outside the focal labour boundary.

The caretaker produces supply request fields item identifier, usable quantity, requested quantity, unit and required date in s1; its 20 full hours include capture. Missing identifiers or unsuitable catalogue entries require manual entry within retained s2 time.
Catalogue administrator maintains existing item, supplier and pack-unit records; no new upstream capture is assumed. Check native saved lists before custom code.
No automatic par-level or diet inference is used; all quantities are selected by the caretaker.
unknowns: Native saved-list support and repetitive order share
Catalogue quality and permission to place orders
research_questions: Does saved-line reuse reduce order entry by 40% after all checks and corrections?

already_counted.description: Order checking, correction and release approval

approvals.approved_version: Final order snapshot: item identifiers, quantities, units, supplier, delivery date, address and total; changes void approval before release

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=94, gross=6 minus 1 upkeep gives net=5. High assumes repeat catalogue orders; low assumes only 1 point of entry saving offsets upkeep. Physical 65 hours and capture 20 remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Discuss needs and select suitable pet food and supplies with customers
Scan selected products, verify prices and take payment at retail checkout
Hand products and receipt to customer and explain relevant care instructions

tasks.design: Keep product selection, checkout and handover with the caretaker. The existing retail checkout in {OTHER} already calculates the sale, so its runtime earns no new labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most work is customer discussion and physical handover, with checkout already supported.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional change is proposed without evidence of duplicate entry.
tasks.still_hard: Product suitability and customer understanding require care.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a product question needs veterinary advice.
tasks.altitude: Selling work and decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: How to distinguish general care information from clinical advice

evidence.claim: Existing checkout arithmetic provides no incremental saving in this unchanged sales design.

assumptions: Boundary is the caretaker's customer sale, excluding stock replenishment and supplier work.
OTHER is the existing retail checkout category. Caretaker scanning and correcting item and quantity inputs remains fully counted in s2; existing catalogue maintenance is unchanged.
Native checkout is already used; no new software or incremental upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Whether this setting sells products and uses a retail checkout
research_questions: Is there duplicated sale entry outside the existing checkout that warrants a separate task study?

already_counted.description: All checkout scanning and verification retained

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, upkeep=0 and net=0. Customer discussion, product handling and current checkout remain unchanged.
